plan.title: Agent meta-architecture — full stack action plan
plan.description: A 5-phase production build plan for a context-window-aware agent that uses its token budget as a control plane for external automation scripts. The agent never writes final code directly — it writes scripts that write the code, runs them, and stores only compressed summaries. This lets a 512-token model build arbitrarily large codebases across many turns.
plan.build_order: strict — each phase must be complete before starting the next
plan.core_principle: The agent is a control plane, not a code writer. It generates Python automation scripts that generate the actual codebase. Each script run can produce tens of thousands of lines. The agent only ever sees compressed summaries of what was built.

phases.label: Memory fabric
phases.description: Build the on-disk memory system that lets a tiny model remember everything across sessions. This is the foundation every other phase depends on.

tasks.name: Create the folder structure on disk
tasks.sub: One-time setup — run a Python script to scaffold directories
tasks.what: You need a set of nested folders that will hold all agent memories, automation scripts, generated code, and indices. This is the physical brain of the system.
tasks.how: Run this Python script once to create the entire directory hierarchy. After this runs, the folder structure exists and every other component has a home.

memory_fabric/.indices/: index files that track every memory and atomic ref

example_project/.user_prompts/: UUID-named JSON files of what the user said
example_project/.agent_outputs/: UUID-named JSON files of what the agent replied

automation/.code_generators/: Python build scripts the agent writes
automation/.schema_templates/: JSON blueprints for different project types

tasks.name: Build the token-aware index manager
tasks.sub: Python class that loads only memories that fit in the token budget
tasks.what: The index manager is what lets a 512-token model selectively pull in only the memories relevant to the current task, scored by recency, frequency, and keyword overlap — so it never wastes context on irrelevant history. It also manages an overflow queue for memories that do not fit.
tasks.how: A Python class called TokenAwareIndex reads master_index.json, scores each stored memory record, and packs the highest-scoring ones into the context budget. The rest are written to an overflow_queue.json for later cycles. Every time a memory is accessed its access_count increments, raising its future score.

key_concepts.token_budget: context_limit minus a reserve for actual processing
key_concepts.scoring: 60% keyword overlap + 25% recency decay + 15% access frequency
key_concepts.overflow_queue: IDs of memories that did not fit, stored for next cycle
key_concepts.content_preview: only first 80 chars of each memory is stored in index — full content lives in the file on disk

code.content:
import json, hashlib, time, pathlib
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from typing import List

@dataclass
class MemoryRecord:
    id: str
    content_preview: str
    file_path: str
    timestamp: float
    access_count: int
    domain: str
    embedding_stub: List[float] = field(default_factory=list)

class TokenAwareIndex:
    INDEX_PATH = pathlib.Path('memory_fabric/indices/master_index.json')
    OVERFLOW_PATH = pathlib.Path('memory_fabric/indices/overflow_queue.json')
    TOKENS_PER_CHAR = 0.25

    def __init__(self, context_limit: int = 512, reserve: int = 150):
        self.context_limit = context_limit
        self.reserve = reserve
        self.budget = context_limit - reserve
        self.records: List[MemoryRecord] = self._load_index()

    def _load_index(self) -> List[MemoryRecord]:
        if not self.INDEX_PATH.exists():
            return []
        raw = json.loads(self.INDEX_PATH.read_text())
        return [MemoryRecord(**r) for r in raw]

    def _estimate_tokens(self, text: str) -> int:
        return max(1, int(len(text) * self.TOKENS_PER_CHAR))

    def _score(self, rec: MemoryRecord, prompt: str) -> float:
        prompt_words = set(prompt.lower().split())
        preview_words = set(rec.content_preview.lower().split())
        overlap = len(prompt_words & preview_words) / max(1, len(prompt_words))
        age_hours = (time.time() - rec.timestamp) / 3600
        recency = 1.0 / (1.0 + age_hours * 0.01)
        freq = min(1.0, rec.access_count * 0.1)
        return (overlap * 0.6) + (recency * 0.25) + (freq * 0.15)

    def get_relevant_memories(self, current_prompt: str) -> List[MemoryRecord]:
        scored = sorted(
            [(rec, self._score(rec, current_prompt)) for rec in self.records],
            key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True
        )
        selected, overflow, token_count = [], [], 0
        for rec, score in scored:
            cost = self._estimate_tokens(rec.content_preview)
            if token_count + cost <= self.budget:
                selected.append(rec)
                rec.access_count += 1
                token_count += cost
            else:
                overflow.append(rec.id)
        self.OVERFLOW_PATH.write_text(json.dumps(overflow, indent=2))
        self._save_index()
        return selected

    def add_memory(self, content: str, domain: str, file_path: str) -> str:
        rid = hashlib.sha1(f'{content}{time.time()}'.encode()).hexdigest()[:12]
        rec = MemoryRecord(
            id=rid,
            content_preview=content[:80],
            file_path=file_path,
            timestamp=time.time(),
            access_count=0,
            domain=domain
        )
        self.records.append(rec)
        self._save_index()
        return rid

    def _save_index(self):
        self.INDEX_PATH.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        data = [vars(r) for r in self.records]
        self.INDEX_PATH.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2))

tasks.name: Build the memory writer
tasks.sub: Every user turn and agent turn gets persisted to disk automatically
tasks.what: Every single time the user says something and the agent responds, both sides get saved to disk with a UUID filename and registered in the index. This is how the model gets permanent memory beyond its context window — the index acts as a searchable pointer system to the full content on disk.
tasks.how: A lightweight MemoryWriter class handles atomic writes to the correct domain folder and then calls TokenAwareIndex.add_memory() to register both the user prompt and agent output in the master index.

code.content:
import uuid, time, json, pathlib
from memory_index_manager import TokenAwareIndex

class MemoryWriter:
    BASE = pathlib.Path('memory_fabric/domains')

    def __init__(self, domain: str):
        self.domain = domain
        self.index = TokenAwareIndex()
        (self.BASE / domain / 'user_prompts').mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        (self.BASE / domain / 'agent_outputs').mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    def save_turn(self, user_text: str, agent_text: str) -> dict:
        turn_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
        ts = time.time()

        up = self.BASE / self.domain / 'user_prompts' / f'{turn_id}.json'
        ao = self.BASE / self.domain / 'agent_outputs' / f'{turn_id}.json'

        up.write_text(json.dumps({'id': turn_id, 'ts': ts, 'text': user_text}, indent=2))
        ao.write_text(json.dumps({'id': turn_id, 'ts': ts, 'text': agent_text}, indent=2))

        self.index.add_memory(user_text, self.domain, str(up))
        self.index.add_memory(agent_text, self.domain, str(ao))

        return {'turn_id': turn_id, 'domain': self.domain}

phases.label: Atomic reference system
phases.description: Every piece of code the agent writes gets a unique calling card stamped into it as a comment. This lets the agent later find, group, and batch-modify specific code blocks across thousands of files without reading all of them.

tasks.name: Define the atomic reference standard
tasks.sub: The comment format stamped into every generated file
tasks.what: Every function, class, and integration point in generated code gets a comment block with 4 fields: a UUID, an integration group ID, a list of expansion ports, and a list of cross-references. The agent uses these to find and edit code without needing the full file in context.
tasks.how: Define the schema as a JSON spec. The comment syntax adapts to the target language — Python uses #, C++ and JS use //. The integration_group field is the key mechanism that lets the agent batch-modify all code sharing a group tag at once.

atomic_ref_fields.uuid: 12-char hex unique ID for this specific block — used for precise single-block targeting
atomic_ref_fields.integration_group: shared tag for blocks that work together — used for batch operations across files
atomic_ref_fields.expansion_ports: named hooks that the expansion runner will later ask the agent to implement
atomic_ref_fields.cross_refs: UUIDs of other atomic blocks this one depends on — used for dependency tracking
atomic_ref_fields.lang: python | cpp | csharp | js | ts | rust | go

tasks.example_injected_python:
# ATOMIC_REF::uuid=a1b2c3d4e5f6

# CROSS_REFS::f7e8d9c0b1a2
# LAYER::logic
def npc_decide_action(npc_state: dict) -> str:
    ...

tasks.name: Build the atomic reference injector
tasks.sub: Python module that stamps any code string with its calling card before writing to disk
tasks.what: Before any generated code hits disk, it passes through the injector which prepends the calling card comment block. This is what makes every line of generated code retrievable and groupable later. The registry is a JSON file that maps UUID to the full AtomicUnit record.
tasks.how: AtomicReferenceSystem.stamp() generates a UUID, builds the header comment in the correct language syntax, prepends it to the code, saves the unit to an atomic_registry.json, and tracks group membership. pull_group_to_context() retrieves all units in a group concatenated — ready to inject into the agent's prompt. batch_replace() can modify thousands of lines across files with a single call.

tasks.name: Build the context window assembler
tasks.sub: Pulls atomic refs and memories into a single trimmed context string for the agent
tasks.what: This is the bridge between the memory system and the agent. Before each agent call, the assembler gathers the most relevant memory previews and requested atomic code blocks, then trims everything to fit inside the token budget — guaranteeing the agent never blows its context limit regardless of how large the memory fabric grows.
tasks.how: ContextAssembler.build() queries TokenAwareIndex for relevant memories, optionally pulls integration groups from AtomicReferenceSystem, and assembles a single string that fits within MAX_TOKENS minus the overhead for the system prompt and user message. The assembled string is wrapped in XML-style tags so the agent knows what is memory versus what is the current request.

phases.label: Automation script engine
phases.description: The agent's core superpower. Instead of writing a 10,000-line game in one turn, it writes a Python automation script in one turn, then that script is run to generate the full codebase. One 512-token output. Infinite scale.

tasks.name: Build the schema interrogator
tasks.sub: Agent outputs a JSON schema of clarifying questions before building anything
tasks.what: Before writing any code, the agent produces a JSON file with blank fields asking for project specifics — genre, mechanics, platforms, systems to include. The user (or another AI) fills it in. This prevents the agent from making wrong assumptions that invalidate the entire generated codebase. The schema also defines which automation language to use and what layers to generate.
tasks.how: Base schema templates for game, software, and AI projects live in /automation/schema_templates/. The agent selects the closest template, adds any project-specific fields, and writes it to disk. The filled schema then drives all code generation in Phase 3.

tasks.name: Build the procedural code generator
tasks.sub: Agent uses its 512 tokens to write a Python script that generates thousands of lines
tasks.what: This is the core mechanic. The agent writes ONE Python automation script per build cycle. That script reads the filled-in project schema and procedurally generates the entire codebase — file by file, function by function — with atomic reference stamps on every block. The agent never writes the final target language code directly. It writes a Python script that writes the C++ or whatever is needed.
tasks.how: The agent outputs a build_PROJECTNAME.py script. When you run it, it generates the full project folder with all files. Every function gets an atomic ref stamped as a comment. Every file gets a manifest entry. Integration points get EXPANSION_PORTS comments telling the expansion runner what to build next. The script is self-contained — it does not import from the agent system, it just produces files.
tasks.what_the_agent_produces_in_512_tokens: A complete Python script that: (1) imports only stdlib, (2) defines stamp() for atomic refs, (3) defines one generate_X() function per major system, (4) writes all output to disk in a projects/ folder, (5) writes a manifest.json summarizing what was built.

code.note: This is an EXAMPLE of what the agent outputs — not what you write. The agent produces this script as its response, then you run it.

tasks.name: Build the script executor and result compressor
tasks.sub: Runs generated scripts and feeds compressed summaries back to the agent
tasks.what: After the agent writes the automation script, ScriptExecutor runs it in a subprocess and captures output. ResultCompressor then reads the manifest and scans expansion port comments to produce a short token-efficient summary the agent can use on the next turn — knowing what was built without re-reading all the code.
tasks.how: ScriptExecutor.run() uses subprocess with a timeout. ResultCompressor.compress() reads manifest.json and scans all generated files for EXPANSION_PORTS comments, producing a 3-line summary that fits in the agent's remaining token budget. This summary becomes the agent's working knowledge of the current project state.

phases.label: Agent control loop
phases.description: Wire everything together into a single orchestration loop. The agent checks memory, picks a build strategy, writes the automation script, runs it, reads the compressed result, and iterates — all automatically.

tasks.name: Build the meta-agent controller
tasks.sub: The main loop that orchestrates every other component
tasks.what: MetaAgentController is the brain. Given a user request, it decides whether to ask clarifying questions (JSON schema output), generate a build script (Python script output), or produce a text reply. It maintains state between turns via the compressed build summaries and saves every turn to memory.
tasks.how: The controller calls your LLM via the adapter interface (any model). It injects the assembled context, receives a response, then routes it by detecting whether the response is a JSON schema, a Python build script, or plain text. Build scripts get run immediately. Results get compressed and stored as the agent's working knowledge of the project.

response_routing_logic.json_schema_detected: save schema to disk, return file path to user to fill in
response_routing_logic.python_build_script_detected: save script, run it, compress results, store in last_build_result
response_routing_logic.plain_text: return directly, save to memory as normal turn

code.content:
import json, pathlib, re
from context_assembler import ContextAssembler
from memory_writer import MemoryWriter
from script_executor import ScriptExecutor, ResultCompressor

class MetaAgentController:
    SCRIPTS_DIR = pathlib.Path('memory_fabric/automation/code_generators')
    PROJECTS_DIR = pathlib.Path('projects')

    def __init__(self, domain: str, llm_caller):
        self.domain = domain
        self.llm = llm_caller
        self.assembler = ContextAssembler(domain)
        self.writer = MemoryWriter(domain)
        self.executor = ScriptExecutor()
        self.compressor = ResultCompressor()
        self.last_build_result: str = ''

    def handle_turn(self, user_input: str, active_groups: list[str] = None) -> str:
        assembled = self.assembler.build(user_input, active_groups or [])
        if self.last_build_result:
            assembled += f'\n<last_build>\n{self.last_build_result}\n</last_build>'

        raw_response = self.llm(assembled)
        result = self._route_response(raw_response, user_input)
        self.writer.save_turn(user_input, result)
        return result

    def _route_response(self, response: str, user_input: str) -> str:
        stripped = response.strip()

        if stripped.startswith('# build_') or 'if __name__' in stripped:
            return self._handle_build_script(stripped)

        try:
            parsed = json.loads(stripped)
            if 'project_type' in parsed:
                schema_path = self.SCRIPTS_DIR / 'schema_in_progress.json'
                schema_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
                schema_path.write_text(json.dumps(parsed, indent=2))
                return f'Schema saved. Fill in blank fields in:\n{schema_path}'
        except (json.JSONDecodeError, KeyError):
            pass

        return response

    def _handle_build_script(self, script_code: str) -> str:
        m = re.search(r'# build_(.+)\.py', script_code)
        project_name = m.group(1) if m else 'unnamed_project'

        script_path = self.SCRIPTS_DIR / f'build_{project_name}.py'
        script_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        script_path.write_text(script_code)

        exec_result = self.executor.run(str(script_path))
        project_path = str(self.PROJECTS_DIR / project_name)
        self.last_build_result = self.compressor.compress(project_path, exec_result)

        status = 'succeeded' if exec_result['success'] else 'failed'
        return f'Build script executed and {status}.\n\n{self.last_build_result}'

tasks.name: Build the expansion cycle runner
tasks.sub: Automated loop that keeps growing the codebase from expansion ports
tasks.what: After the first build, the codebase has hundreds of EXPANSION_PORTS comments. The expansion cycle feeds those port names back to the agent one integration group at a time, asking it to generate the next automation script for each. This is how a 512-token model builds arbitrarily large software across many turns — each turn targets one expansion port, produces one script, runs it, advances the project.
tasks.how: ExpansionRunner scans the project for all EXPANSION_PORTS comments, collects unique (group, port) tuples, and processes them one at a time. For each, it pulls the relevant atomic group code into context and prompts the agent to expand that specific port. The agent writes an expansion script, which gets run, which adds more stamped code with new expansion ports — the cycle continues.
tasks.scaling_note: Each expansion cycle uses only the tokens needed for one atomic group (typically 50-150 tokens of code) plus the expansion port name — leaving the agent plenty of budget to write the next automation script. This is how you get 50,000+ lines from a 512-token model.

phases.label: IDE integration and scaling
phases.description: Connect everything to your existing IDE agent. Add multi-drive memory routing, model-swap support, and a plain-English CLI so you can drive the whole system without touching code.

tasks.name: Build the drive router
tasks.sub: Hot, warm, and cold memory tiers across multiple physical drives
tasks.what: The memory fabric needs to span multiple drives as you described. Recent memories stay on the fastest drive. Older memories migrate to secondary storage. Very old memories go to archival storage. The index manager queries across all three transparently — the calling code never needs to know which drive a file is on.
tasks.how: DriveRouter wraps path resolution based on file age. When the index manager retrieves a file path, DriveRouter.resolve() checks all three tiers in order and returns the actual physical path. promote_or_demote() should be called periodically (e.g. on a daily cron or each time the index is saved) to migrate files between tiers as they age.

tier_thresholds.hot: last 7 days — fastest drive (NVMe, RAM disk, or fastest SSD)
tier_thresholds.warm: 7-30 days — secondary drive (slower SSD or secondary NVMe)
tier_thresholds.cold: 30+ days — archival drive (HDD, external drive, or cloud-backed storage)

tasks.name: Build the model-swap adapter
tasks.sub: Any LLM plugs in as a drop-in replacement without changing any other code
tasks.what: Your IDE can connect to different models. The adapter pattern means you define one interface and any model — local via Ollama, remote via Anthropic API, OpenAI, or any other provider — plugs in as a drop-in. The entire rest of the system stays unchanged when you swap models.
tasks.how: Abstract base class LLMAdapter with a single call() method. Concrete subclasses implement the actual HTTP call for each provider. Pass an adapter instance into MetaAgentController and the whole system works with whatever model is behind it.
supported_providers: OpenAI API — add OpenAIAdapter following same pattern

tasks.name: Build the CLI entry point
tasks.sub: Plain English commands to drive the entire system from terminal
tasks.what: A single Python script you run from terminal. You type what you want in plain English. It routes to the right component — building, expanding, querying memory, checking status — without you needing to know which class handles it. This is your primary interface to the whole system.
tasks.how: argparse CLI with three modes: single-message mode (--message), expansion mode (--expand), and interactive REPL. Supports any model via --model and --api-key flags.
usage_examples: python agent_cli.py --model mistral --message "build an RPG game in C++"
python agent_cli.py --model mistral  (no --message = interactive REPL mode)

tasks.name: Build the system prompt template for the agent
tasks.sub: The instruction set that tells the agent how to behave in script-generation mode
tasks.what: The agent needs a system prompt that instructs it to operate in script-generation mode — when to produce JSON schemas, when to produce Python build scripts, and how to stamp atomic references. Without this, the model will just write conversational replies instead of actionable automation.
tasks.how: A plain text file that gets prepended to every assembled context. It instructs the model on the three response modes and the exact comment format for atomic refs.

code.content:
You are a meta-agent operating in script-generation mode. You do not write final code directly. You write Python automation scripts that generate final code.

You have three valid response types:

1. JSON SCHEMA — when you need clarification before building. Output ONLY a raw JSON object with blank fields for the user to fill in. Always include: project_type, name, target_language, automation_language, description, and a layers array.

2. PYTHON BUILD SCRIPT — when you have enough information to build. Output ONLY a complete, runnable Python script. The script filename comment must be on line 1 in format: # build_PROJECTNAME.py. The script must: import only stdlib, define a stamp() function that prepends atomic ref comments, define one generate_X() function per system, write all output to a projects/PROJECTNAME/ folder, and write a manifest.json at the end.

3. PLAIN TEXT — only for direct questions about status, memory, or architecture that do not require building.

ATOMIC REF FORMAT — every generated code block must begin with:
# ATOMIC_REF::uuid=<12hexchars>
# INTEGRATION_GROUP::<group_name>
# EXPANSION_PORTS::<port1,port2 or none>
# CROSS_REFS::<uuid1,uuid2 or none>
# LAYER::<data|logic|ui|test|infra>

When you see <memory> tags, those are your past memories. Use them to maintain continuity.
When you see <last_build> tags, that is a summary of what was built last cycle. Build on top of it.
Never explain what you are about to do. Just produce the output.

tasks.name: Wire the system prompt into the controller
tasks.sub: Update MetaAgentController to prepend system_prompt.txt to every LLM call
tasks.what: The controller needs to load the system prompt and prepend it to every assembled context before calling the LLM. This is a small edit to meta_agent_controller.py.
tasks.how: Add a _load_system_prompt() method and prepend its content in handle_turn() before calling self.llm().

tasks.name: Build the periodic maintenance script
tasks.sub: Cron-runnable script that migrates memory tiers and prunes the index
tasks.what: As the memory fabric grows, the index file will grow. The maintenance script runs periodically (daily or weekly via cron or Task Scheduler) to migrate files between hot/warm/cold tiers and prune any index records pointing to deleted files.
tasks.how: A standalone script that loads the index, instantiates DriveRouter with your actual drive paths, calls migrate_all(), removes stale records, and saves the cleaned index. Configure HOT_PATH, WARM_PATH, COLD_PATH to your actual drive mount points.

code.content:
import json, pathlib
from memory_index_manager import TokenAwareIndex
from drive_router import DriveRouter

# CONFIGURE THESE TO YOUR ACTUAL DRIVE PATHS
HOT_PATH  = 'memory_fabric/hot'
WARM_PATH = 'memory_fabric/warm'
COLD_PATH = 'memory_fabric/cold'

def run_maintenance():
    index = TokenAwareIndex()
    router = DriveRouter(HOT_PATH, WARM_PATH, COLD_PATH)

    # Migrate files to correct tier based on last access
    initial_count = len(index.records)
    router.migrate_all([vars(r) for r in index.records])

    # Prune records pointing to deleted files
    before = len(index.records)
    index.records = [
        r for r in index.records
        if router.resolve(r.file_path).exists()
    ]
    pruned = before - len(index.records)

    index._save_index()
    print(f'Maintenance complete.')
    print(f'  Records before: {initial_count}')
    print(f'  Pruned stale records: {pruned}')
    print(f'  Records after: {len(index.records)}')

if __name__ == '__main__':
    run_maintenance()

file_manifest.description: Every file to create, in build order

how_it_works_end_to_end.step_1_first_run: Run scaffold_memory_fabric.py once to create all directories
how_it_works_end_to_end.step_3_user_asks_to_build: You type: build me an RPG game in C++
how_it_works_end_to_end.step_4_agent_asks_questions: Agent outputs a JSON schema. Fill in the blank fields and save it.
how_it_works_end_to_end.step_5_agent_writes_build_script: Tell the agent the schema is filled. It outputs a Python build script in one 512-token response.
how_it_works_end_to_end.step_6_script_runs: The controller automatically runs the script. It generates thousands of lines of C++ across dozens of files.
how_it_works_end_to_end.step_7_compressed_result: ResultCompressor produces a 3-line summary of what was built and what expansion ports remain.
how_it_works_end_to_end.step_8_agent_sees_summary: On the next turn, the agent sees only the compressed summary — not the actual code. It writes the next expansion script.
how_it_works_end_to_end.step_9_loop: Steps 5-8 repeat automatically via expansion_runner.py until all EXPANSION_PORTS are implemented.
how_it_works_end_to_end.step_10_memory_persists: Every turn is saved to disk. Restart the session and the agent picks up exactly where it left off.

scaling_rules.512_token_models: Tight compression. Memory previews: 80 chars max. Build scripts: one system per script. Max 5 expansion ports per cycle.
scaling_rules.4k_token_models: Relaxed compression. Can hold more memory previews. Build scripts can generate 3-5 systems at once.
scaling_rules.32k_plus_models: Minimal compression. Can hold full atomic group code, not just previews. Can run multiple expansion cycles in one turn.
scaling_rules.model_swap: Change --model flag. No other code changes needed. The adapter pattern handles the rest.
scaling_rules.automation_language: Always Python regardless of target language. Python can shell out to compilers, write C++/C#/Rust/JS files, and run tests.
scaling_rules.target_language: Any. The build scripts use Python string templates to generate C++, C#, Rust, JS, TypeScript, React, SQL, etc.
